idea: build a blanket fort and watch a favourite childhood movie.
description: Every cushion. Every sheet. Inside the fort, no phones, only old movies, snacks, and silly nonsense.

idea: a five-pound market challenge.
description: Five pounds each, twenty minutes. The catch: we have to make dinner from whatever the other person brings home. Inventiveness rewarded.

idea: take a pottery class and keep the ugly mug forever.
description: We will not be good at it. That's the point. The shittiest one is the one we keep — it'll be the best mug we own in five years.

idea: cook a meal from a country neither of us has visited.
description: Three courses, the right music, and let's be real — probably only one course. Pretend we're somewhere else for the evening.

idea: wander a cultural event in the evening.
description: Lots of places host late-night things sometimes — wine, weird lighting, far fewer children. Wear something nice. Make up backstories for the strangers.

idea: be a tourist in our own city.
description: Pick like three attractions we've never bothered with. Buy a tacky souvenir. Take photos like we've never been here. We haven't, really.

idea: picnic in a nice garden and read aloud.
description: Bring a book — the sillier or cooler the better. Get the picky bits. Trade off chapters until the sun moves.

idea: find an arcade and host a tournament.
description: Loser buys dessert. Skee-ball is a serious sport here. Air hockey is allowed but only with full commitment.

idea: set an absurd alarm and watch the sunrise.
description: Brew coffee (and hot chocolate) in a thermos. Go to the highest point we can reach. Sit there until the sky changes colour.

idea: bake a pie and deliver it to a friend.
description: No need to warn them. The pie doesn't have to be good. The visit will be.

idea: charity-shop outfit swap, ten pounds each.
description: Thirty minutes, ten pounds, one shop. Dress each other for an imaginary occasion. The more specific the imagined occasion, the better the outfit.

idea: find an outdoor cinema.
description: There is one, somewhere, within reacheable distance. Probably. Bring snacks they would never sell at any concession stand.

idea: take a couples' dance class — pick the one that scares you.
description: Salsa, swing, tango. One lesson is enough to make you laugh at me for the rest of the evening. Two and we might actually like it.

idea: day trip to the town with the funniest name.
description: Look at a map. Pick the town with the silliest name within an hour. Go there. Eat at the chippy. Look at the church. Leave.

idea: find a poetry reading or open mic and go.
description: Whisper our reactions only when no one is looking. Buy a drink. Stay for the whole thing — the last reader is always the most interesting.

idea: hunt the charity shop for the strangest object.
description: Five pounds max, twenty minutes on the clock. Buy each other something useless and beautiful. Display it proudly. Forever.

idea: project a film onto our ceiling.
description: Sheet, projector, an extension cord that's testing its limits. Mindless entertainment is the only correct answer. Snacks compulsory.

idea: empty karaoke room, the earlier the better.
description: Three in the afternoon on a Tuesday. The room is ours. Sing badly, sing loudly, sing every song you ever loved at fourteen.

idea: a nice walk, a nice podcast.
description: Decide on a trail. Pick a podcast we've both been meaning to start. Walk until the episode ends. Stop where we stand. Find food.

idea: synchronised film night — press play on three.
description: Text reactions throughout. Pretend we're sitting on the same couch. Pause for snacks at the same time.

idea: same recipe, two kitchens, also two cameras.
description: Pick a recipe neither of us has tried. Cook it in parallel over video call. Critique generously. Eat together when it's all done.

idea: a co-op video game made for two.
description: It Takes Two and Stardew Valley were built for this. Overcooked, if we want to test our relationship. Choose wisely.

idea: tour a museum from our couches.
description: The Louvre, the Met, the Smithsonian — all free, all online. The more niche the museum, the better.

idea: show and tell — three weird possessions each.
description: Defend their honour. Vote on the strangest. The story behind it matters more than the object itself; that's always true.

idea: take an online language class and be terrible together.
description: Pick a language neither of us speaks. Weird Youtube video is best. Embarassing yet fun.

idea: build a shared playlist, turn by turn.
description: Take turns adding songs. No skipping. The rules are sacred. The playlist will be strange and personal and exactly right.

idea: truth or drink — or truth or tea.
description: There's a deck for this. Or just make up the questions. Drinks are optional; the questions are the whole point.

idea: virtual paint night with the same reference.
description: Same reference photo, two attempts, no peeking. Reveal at the end. The worse we are at painting, the better this works.

idea: walk a foreign city via street view.
description: Pick a city we'd both like to visit (but likely will not). Walk the streets together from our couches. Make notes for the real trip we'll never take.

idea: documentary watch-along, with pauses.
description: Pause every twenty minutes to discuss. Pick something niche — obscure history works best. Surprise ourselves with what you both know. Or don't

idea: serious online game, video on, trash talk allowed.
description: Scrabble, chess, I can't think of others right now. Keep the camera on. Half the game are the faces we make unintentionally.

idea: solve a virtual escape room together.
description: There are lots of these now. Pick one, share a screen, don't Google the answers. The arguing is the whole pleasure.

idea: co-write a story, one sentence at a time.
description: Open a Google Doc. Take turns. End up somewhere strange (though likely gay). The rule is: no editing each other's sentences. Only adding.

idea: karaoke over video — commit.
description: Smule exists. So does just queueing up YouTube karaoke and embarrassing ourselves. The trick is going first.

idea: take a weird class together.
description: Pick the most absurd one; free, of course. Commit to one full lesson. Take notes. Learning is enrichment.

idea: plan an imaginary (for now) trip in detail.
description: Shared Pinterest board. Make an itinerary. Cost it out. We wont't go. Or maybe we will someday! Either way, it's a real evening together.

idea: trivia night — just the two of us.
description: Free apps abound. Or take turns asking questions on a chosen topic. The arguments over the answers are better than the questions.

idea: get the same lego set and race.
description: Build together over video. The first one done has to plan the next date. The slower one usually does it better, anyway.

idea: read a chapter aloud to each other.
description: Take turns. Find a book that makes us both smile. Even ten minutes occasionally is enough; it'll last weeks. That's the point.

idea: an hour-long photo scavenger hunt.
description: Make a list together. We each take an hour to find everything around our house or neighbourhood. Reveal photos at the end. Score generously.

idea: tarot night — believe or don't.
description: One reads, the other listens. Switch. Believe none of it, or all of it. The cards are mostly an excuse to talk about our week.

idea: watch the same weird youtube rabbit hole.
description: Pick a topic — competitive duck herding, Soviet animation, anything. Take turns sending the next video. Time passes instantly.
